# The RT64 shaders the web page builds: one shader description a line, other mode L and H, color combiner L and H,
# flags, in hex. RT64 specializes each one's WGSL when the page is built and builds them with the game waiting: those
# above the first "section" line before the game starts, and a level's section when the level first draws with its
# shaders, so that nothing draws with the ubershader, which integrated graphics can't afford (N64Recomp-browser's
# README, "Give RT64 a list of the game's shaders").
#
# Recorded by code, not by playing: bash tools/record_shaders.sh (its header says how) runs N64Recomp-browser's
# tools/record_shaders.mjs with tools/shader_plan.json, which loads the page fresh for each section and has
# patches/shader_survey.c show each menu and start each level. Section 0 is the launcher, the boot as it plays by
# itself until the first attract demo (the logos, the cast credits, the gun barrel and the title: later rounds of
# the cast draw nothing new), the menus, a mission's briefing and its report; then a section a level, from its
# opening cutscene to a few seconds in, walking, turning, firing and opening the watch. Jungle, Control, Caverns,
# Aztec and Egypt, whose guards and rooms further in draw shaders their starts don't, are played again in a load of
# their own, Bond invincible (tools/shader_survey.js), about 45 s past the cutscene: forward and back by as much,
# turning, strafing, firing, aiming, changing weapon and opening doors, with the guards that come for him fought.
# Not recorded: the multiplayer levels, the attract demos, and what the other levels draw further in than their
# starts (RT64 builds those when the game first asks for them). Flags follow settings (filtering, HDR, MSAA,
# upscaling), so a change to one of those defaults means recording again.
